text:
alex: Seeing intermittent gRPC streaming stalls between pods on node pairs in us-west2-prod. Starts around the 10:20 deploy. Errors look like stalled recv, then reconnects.

maria: ugh. any packet drops visible on the nodes?

alex: small repro: stream a 3MB payload, about ~1.2s in the stream pauses for ~4-6s then resumes. tcpdump shows retransmits, and I see ICMP "fragmentation needed" on node A -> node B.

jordan_b: ICMP frag-needed? cloud VPC usually allows that but some firewall rules can drop it. can you paste the tcpdump snippet?

alex: here — trimmed:
```
14:12:05.123456 IP 10.10.23.45.54321 > 10.10.42.66.50051: Flags [P.], seq 1:1201, ack 1, win 29200, length 1200
14:12:05.123789 IP 10.10.42.66 > 10.10.23.45: ICMP 3/4 frag needed and DF set, mtu 1400
14:12:09.223111 IP 10.10.23.45.54321 > 10.10.42.66.50051: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 29200, length 511
```

maria: mtu 1400 — we run vxlan with overlay mtu 1450 historically. did the node image change?

samir: also seeing RDMA nodes intermittently flapping in the same window. If RDMA/InfiniBand is enabled and overlay MTU is lower, kernel offload/GSO interaction can lead to weird reassembly behavior.

ajordan_b: good call. alex, what's `ip link` on the node pair?

alex: on node A (sender): `eth0 mtu 9000`, `vxlan0 mtu 1450`, pod veth mtu 1400. On node B (receiver): `eth0 mtu 1500`, `vxlan0 mtu 1500`, pod veth mtu 1500. So mismatch.

maria: oh nice catch. one side was auto-upgraded to new kernel/networking config during maintenance. overlay mtu bumped on B, left A at 1450.

samir: that explains the frag-needed. ICMP tells sender to lower packet size to 1400 but if ICMP gets dropped (some nets drop ICMP type 3 code 4) you get blackholing/pmtu-probe hangs. gRPC streaming especially sensitive because it holds long-lived connections and relies on TCP progress.

alex: quick workaround: reduced gRPC max frame size at client to 1KB and that eliminated stalls in the canary. but want permanent fix.

jordan_b: options: 1) standardize overlay MTU across nodes (best), 2) enable PMTU blackhole detection on kernels (`sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`), 3) ensure ICMP/DF isn't being dropped on firewall, 4) tune GSO/TSO offloading for vxlan on RDMA hosts.

maria: schedule config sync to push vxlan mtu=1450 to node B to match A? or set both to 1500 if underlying can support jumbo. which is safer?

samir: if any link in path can't handle 9000, safer to normalize to 1450 (typical for cloud overlays). Also enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 until we can confirm ICMP flows.

alex: I'll roll a hotfix daemonset to set `ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1450` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` across us-west2-prod. will monitor.

replies later:

srebot: Deploy triggered: hotfix-daemonset/us-west2-prod (deployment id: dfc-2026-03-18-045).

(alex 10m later): hotfix rolled to 90% nodes. preliminary metrics: gRPC stall incidents down from ~23 -> 2 in the first 15m.

maria: nice. can we add an alert that cross-node `vxlan mtu` drift > 0 triggers a config drift ticket?

jordan_b: yes, we'll add a k8s-node-probe that compares `ip link` MTU on all enis/vxlan against desired config and creates a perf alert. I'll own the ticket.

samir: follow-up: on RDMA-enabled nodes we should also disable GRO/GSO on the vxlan interface if kernel+hw offload cause packet reassembly bugs. I'll test.

alex: thanks team. lesson: small MTU mismatches + dropped ICMP -> gRPC streaming SNAFUs.

deploy-bot: hotfix-daemonset completed - rollout 100% (dfc-2026-03-18-045). :white_check_mark:

(jordan_b 40m later): created infra ticket INFRA-4821: "Detect and reconcile overlay MTU drift (vxlan/encap)" and PR linked for a node-prober + alerting.

maria: closing the thread from monitoring POV once alerts are in and RDMA test results are green. :thumbsup:
